newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-Czech bourse bans members'off-mkt OTC trades.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Czech bourse bans members'off-mkt OTC trades.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) governing board took another major step in its battle to improve market transparency on Tuesday when it agreed to force its members to trade exclusively on organised markets.

The new rule, effective on August 1, bans member brokerages -- which do most of Czech securities trading -- from the widespread practice of over-the-counter trades simply recorded at the Central Securities Registry (SCP).

"Members of the bourse must trade in securities only on organised markets," PSE Chamber chairman Tomas Jezek told a news conference. "The impact of the change has the character of strengthening the central price-making market."
The move would still allow OTC trades to be made if they are registered directly with the PSE.
But the bourse chamber also agreed to, in effect, hike transaction fees on the direct block trades to encourage more market-maker activity.

The chamber agreed that fees for direct trades registered at the Prague Stock Exchange would be proportional to total turnover and no longer a simple flat fee, while transaction fees for trades on the central market would be lowered, Jezek said.

Jezek has been fighting for tighter regulation of the opaque capital markets for a long time, and has backed several measures to promote transparency and consolidate PSE trade since becoming its chairman last year.
Bourse members are currently obliged to report trades they conduct over-the-counter to the PSE.
Some members of the stock exchange welcomed the measure, saying it will help to strenghten the market-maker role of the PSE's central trading system.

"I think it is a step in the right direction. Securities have been being transferred for prices at which they were not trading on the PSE nor in the (retail-oriented) RM-System," said Karel Bastl of Atlantik Financial Markets.
The rule would still allow PSE members, numbering more than 100 firms, to conduct trades through the low volume, storefront RM-System, the country's other organised bourse.
The PSE has been taking steps to concentrate more trading on its central market and limit the OTC trades which still dominate turnover in Czech securities.
Czech OTC trades have been frequently criticised for questionable pricing methods and poor transparency, while activity on Prague's two organised markets has remained relatively thin.
Petr Koblic of investment bank Patria Finance said he was not happy about the increase of direct trade fees.
"That means that when you ban trades at the SCP, you can increase your own prices, which is the negative part of this process," he told Reuters.
He noted that prices on the PSE's automated central market were often irrellevant as it was often created only by "a couple of shares".
Still, that is a major reason many analysts would like to see an increase of activity on the central bourse.
